statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies Registry online filing portal administered by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or the Samoan language. Local script is accepted only where a transliteration in Roman characters is provided; Chinese characters and non-Roman scripts are not permitted in the formal registered name. A direct English-language or transliterated equivalent must be used for all statutory filings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must state the legal basis for distinctiveness and compliance with the International Companies Act. The Registrar issues a written determination within 14 days. If the administrative appeal is refused, judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa must be filed within 30 days of the refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office is not permissible for an International Company incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987. The company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa, which may be the office of the licensed registered agent. A virtual address without a physical presence does not satisfy the statutory requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but active: approximately 2% annual risk-based probability of unannounced inspection by the Registrar or the Financial Intelligence Unit across the international companies portfolio. The Medium_Risk_Enhanced classification of a voice streaming social app may elevate targeted inspection probability during the first year of operation.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; International Company may issue a single no-par value share. There is no escrow account or capital deposit requirement under Samoa law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers named in the Memorandum and Articles of Association are hereby confirmed as the founding shareholders and the allotment of one ordinary no-par value share to each subscriber is ratified. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name of Director 1] and [Name of Director 2] are appointed as the first directors of the Company, and that [Name of Officer] is appointed as Secretary/Director, each to serve until the next annual general meeting and until their successors are elected. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) Registry Window, Apia Central Business District.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a SIFSA-licensed registered agent to conduct a name availability search. Submit Form IC-NameRes with the proposed entity name and company object. The registered agent signs a letter of engagement and files the reservation request online or in person. After reservation, the name is held for 30 days pending full incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Identity and residential address of each proposed director
Certified copy of the registered agent's license
Letter of engagement with the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses the name, file a written appeal within 14 days with SIFSA's Registry Department or submit a new name reservation within the same fee window. A decision is given in 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent submits the duly executed Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form IC-1 to SIFSA's international desk. The government fee of USD 200 is tendered via bank transfer or approved electronic gateway. Supporting director consents and registered office confirmation are lodged simultaneously. All documents must be notarized where required by SIFSA practice.
required_dossiers: Drafted and executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Written consent to act as director from each proposed director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFSA issues a requisition letter, the registered agent has 30 days to provide explanatory or corrective documentation. If the issue is cured, the application proceeds; if not, the application lapses and a fresh filing is required with the same fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Opening of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon final review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under the International Companies Act 2017. The company must then open statutory registers — members, directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners (if applicable) — and file the notice of registered office form with SIFSA within 14 days. The certificate is retrieved by the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Receipt of paid government incorporation fees
Registered office address confirmation from the licensed agent
Statutory register templates and opening entries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is withheld due to administrative backlog, the registered agent may file a written expedite request with SIFSA requiring action within 3 business days. If the statutory register is filed late, file a late filing rectification statement and pay a USD 50 reinstatement fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Compliance and Non-Industrial Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFSA Licensing Section; Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Trade and Industry Licensing Division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, submit a copy of the Certificate of Incorporation and registered agent details to SIFSA's licensing database. For the pure digital voice-streaming activity, no industrial operating license is required under Samoa law. If the company later establishes a physical office, file an occupational premises notification with MCIL. Optionally, file a tax-exempt status application with the Ministry of Revenue if the International Company elects offshore tax treatment.
required_dossiers: Tax exemption application (optional, if International Company status is elected)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFSA or MCIL queries the filing, the registered agent has 21 days to resubmit the missing information. Late filing of the tax exemption or business registration is subject to a maximum penalty of 20 Samoa Tala per day; an appeal may be lodged with the appropriate institution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Trade and Industry Licensing Division (not applicable to mobile application services).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required; no physical manufacturing, warehouse, or industrial plant. Standard Samoa business registration suffices.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Samoa Environment Protection Agency (SEPA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not triggered. If incidental office waste is generated, comply with the Waste Management Act 2005 and standard municipal disposal codes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a pure online operation; if an office is established, obtain a fire evacuation certificate and workplace sanitation clearance from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority and the Ministry of Labour.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR; Matagaluega o Tupe Maua) of the Independent State of Samoa, the consolidated tax and customs administration; taxpayer e-services portal: Samoa Revenue Online Services (SROS), www.revenue.gov.ws. The Samoa International Company Registry (Registrar of International and Foreign Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour) issues the IC registration number used for tax-exemption administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A pure offshore Samoa International Company (IC) is statutorily exempt from Samoan income tax and VAGST and is not required to obtain a TIN or VAGST ID; the IC registration number and annual Government fee receipt serve as the tax-identity bundle. If the IC creates a Samoan nexus (local branch, Samoan-source income, or taxable supplies to Samoan consumers), it must file the Ministry for Revenue business-registration application (Form T/R-1) via SROS or in person, attaching the IC certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles (or charter), registered-agent and registered-office confirmation, identification of directors and ultimate beneficial owners, and, if applicable, the resident agent undertaking. The Commissioner issues a TIN within 14-30 days, and VAGST registration is mandatory on the same application once a rolling 12-month taxable turnover reaches or is expected to reach WST 100,000. No minimum capital requirement applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no check-the-box election. The IC's Tax_Exempt_Zone status is automatic under the International Companies Act 1987: exemption from income tax on offshore income, no capital gains tax, no stamp duty on offshore instruments, and no VAGST on non-Samoan supplies; the IC pays a fixed annual Government fee instead of income tax. The IC may elect (irrevocably) to re-domesticate to a company under the Companies Act 2001 or to obtain a licence to carry on business in Samoa, thereby entering the domestic income-tax and VAGST net for Samoan-source activities. No hybrid-mismatch election is recognised; the Tax Administration Act 2015 general anti-avoidance rule re-characterises hybrid or conduit arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) — Samoa's VAT system under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 1992, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (SAT 100,000) of taxable supplies in any rolling 12-month period; registration is compulsory once the threshold is met or expected to be met, with voluntary registration at the Commissioner's discretion. For the offshore voice-streaming IC, no threshold is triggered because the supplies of digital audio and companion services through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing are supplied for consumption entirely outside Samoa and no VAGST is chargeable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None: Samoa does not operate a real-time electronic-invoicing clearance, continuous transaction control, fiscal API, or digital stamping regime. Registered persons may issue paper or electronic tax invoices that satisfy the content rules (supplier name and TIN, recipient TIN, date, description, quantity, consideration, VAGST rate and amount), and commercial records must be retained for at least 7 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAGST) applies to: (i) goods removed physically from Samoa under an accepted Customs export entry; and (ii) services supplied to a non-resident recipient where the services are performed outside Samoa and not enjoyed in Samoa. The voice-streaming social app supplies remote digital services (interactive audio chatrooms and companion features) to non-resident end users through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing; these qualify as exported services if the supplier evidences non-residence of the recipient, consumption outside Samoa, settlement in foreign currency via the platform, and consistent commercial paperwork. The supplier must not recover input VAGST attributable to exempt supplies and must separately identify zero-rated exports in its VAGST return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Samoa Customs Service export entry) for physical goods
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical dispatch of goods from Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advices evidencing receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency within the CBS repatriation period
Zero-rated tax invoice, commercial contract, and sales order

For digital services: Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlement statements, monthly sales reports, and non-resident status evidence of the counterparty or end users (foreign business registration, foreign VAT or equivalent ID, or passport)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: MfR audits of zero-rated digital-service exporters concentrate on commercial substance: platform settlement reports, subscriber and usage geo-location data, and foreign-currency receipts must independently corroborate each zero-rated supply. A disallowed zero-rating claim gives rise to an assessed VAGST clawback plus a shortfall penalty of 100% of the shortfall for deliberate evasion, 40% for gross carelessness, or 20% for failure to take reasonable care, with monthly late-payment interest. Fraudulent export zero-rating is a criminal offence under the Tax Administration Act 2015 (fines up to WST 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years), the Commissioner may raise a jeopardy assessment, the four-year reassessment window applies, and directors and beneficial owners of the IC may be jointly and severally assessed where the IC is a mere facade. Non-repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days additionally exposes the exporter to Central Bank of Samoa exchange-control penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) is the sole exchange-control authority, acting under the Exchange Control Ordinance 1961 and CBS Exchange Control Notices/Manual issued to authorized dealers. The Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) separately administers the International Companies Act 1987, under which the WS_IC is incorporated as a non-resident, tax-exempt International Company. Transactions touching Samoan Tala (WST) must flow through CBS-authorized dealers; non-resident IC transactions in USD conducted entirely offshore are exempt from CBS approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: WST is non-convertible on capital account; current-account payments may be processed through authorized dealers with documentary support. The WS_IC earns all revenue offshore in USD (Apple IAP and Google Play Billing proceeds), keeps a foreign-currency account, and pays no Samoan taxes; therefore WST convertibility and profit-remittance controls are structurally avoided. If the IC were a resident company, distributions to non-residents would attract dividend withholding tax under the Income Tax Act 2012 and CBS capital-transfer approval; the International Company exemption eliminates both hurdles. Practical rule: ring-fence revenue in USD, never settle in WST, and maintain no Samoan-resident counterparties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender obligation applies to the WS_IC. Samoa's exchange-control surrender rules target resident exporters of physical goods, who must repatriate export proceeds within the periods prescribed in CBS exchange-control guidelines for the relevant export class and offer conversion into WST at the applicable ratio. Digital-services income of a non-resident International Company is not 'Samoa export proceeds'; Apple/Google remit net USD directly to the IC's foreign-currency account with zero conversion requirement. To preserve this exemption, the IC must earn no Samoan-source income, hold no WST revenue, and direct all app-store payouts to its USD corporate account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational USD Corporate Account (multi-currency, SWIFT-enabled)
Operational Account (USD subject to authorized-dealer confirmation)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: LOW-MEDIUM — viable only as a secondary settlement rail, not as the primary payout account for Apple/Google. Samoa has no domestic EMI licensing regime; the IC must use offshore EMIs (e.g., Payoneer, Airwallex, PingPong, Wise Business). Most offshore EMIs classify Samoa International Companies as high-risk offshore vehicles and reject consumer social/voice-chat apps due to digital-goods AML exposure; where accepted, EMIs impose transaction caps, settlement holds, and UBO EDD equal to bank standards. Apple IAP and Google Play Billing payout engines prefer commercial-bank SWIFT beneficiaries, and an EMI account may be rejected at payout registration because EMIs cannot issue a conventional SWIFT BIC/IBAN in the entity's name. Recommendation: maintain a BSP Samoa USD account as the primary rail and use an EMI only for gateway settlement or regional contractor payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A licensed Samoa registered agent and registered office in Apia are mandatory for the WS_IC. CBS-supervised enhanced due diligence applies to all directors, signatories, and UBOs. Physical attendance in Samoa is generally required for first-time account opening; however, BSP has accepted hybrid remote EDD for non-resident ICs where the director/UBO completes a live video interview, presents an original notarized and apostilled passport, supplies home-bank reference letters, and the Samoa registered agent countersigns the attestation in person. China-resident UBOs should budget 4–8 weeks for EDD; fully remote opening without a qualified professional introducer is not guaranteed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore-vehicle tax-evasion pattern: China tax-resident UBO controls a Samoa tax-exempt IC collecting consumer digital payments via Apple/Google without visible operating substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PRC SAFE ODI/37号文 registration or lawful personal remittance evidence; 12 months of IC financial statements; operating-substance file (Apple Developer Program agreement, Google Play Console registration, cloud-hosting contracts, IP assignments, trademark certificates, contractor agreements); UBO PRC tax filings and asset-origin documentation for injected capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume micro-transaction laundering: large volumes of small in-app purchases with chargeback volatility, consistent with digital-content layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly Apple/Google payout remittance advices reconciled to account statements; platform anti-fraud and KYC controls (user identity verification, device intelligence, spend-velocity monitoring, chargeback management); adopted AML/CFT manual with transaction-threshold alerts; quarterly transaction reporting and annual independent AML audit commitments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell-company opacity: nominee directors, no local staff, no physical assets in Samoa, and family-trust ownership layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SIFA Certificate of Good Standing; statutory registers of directors, shareholders, and charges; registered-agent compliance letter under the International Companies Act 1987; real-economy proof (app analytics, user base, headcount, payroll, server invoices); full trust-instrument disclosure with direct/indirect UBO identification and independent legal opinion on beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP and China-nexus screening hits: common-name matches, family-trust structures, or residual geographic risk from a China-based user base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO PEP/sanctions self-declaration with independent adverse-media and sanctions database search at signing and annually; app geolocation and IP-range documentation confirming no operations in prohibited jurisdictions; explanation of any historical name matches; board resolution confirming sanctions compliance and prohibition of proceeds from sanctioned regions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial capital should arrive as a single named USD wire from the UBO or a documented group financing entity, using SWIFT MT103 with purpose code for equity contribution/share capital. Protocol: (1) board resolution authorizing share issuance and designating the receiving account; (2) UBO completes lawful outbound filings in the home jurisdiction (for PRC residents, SAFE 37号文 registration or a permitted individual remittance within the annual quota — never split wires into structuring tranches); (3) loan/shareholder agreement evidencing arm's-length terms if debt; (4) the receiving bank obtains a Capital Introduction Letter, Certificate of Incorporation, certificate of incumbency, and source-of-funds file; (5) CBS reporting of the inward non-resident transfer is discharged by the bank at crediting, with funds posted in USD without WST conversion. No statutory minimum capital applies to the WS_IC, but the bank expects initial capital commensurate with operating projections; notify the bank 5 business days before the wire to pre-clear EDD.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for all operating payments: Apple developer fees, Google Play registration, cloud/bandwidth hosting, legal, accounting, and contractor salaries. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are disproportionate for pure digital services and are only relevant if the IC later procures licensed hardware or broadcast content. Recurring outflows should remain USD-denominated to preserve the natural hedge, with purchase-order references and ISIC 6311-aligned purpose codes. The bank should receive a standing whitelist of recurring originators (Apple, Google, cloud providers, payroll processors) to reduce false sanctions hits; inbound Apple/Google payout cycles typically settle monthly in USD. Approved dividends of the non-resident IC are paid gross with no Samoan withholding tax, supported by board resolution and the tax-exemption certificate at each remittance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla USD/WST forward contracts through BSP Samoa as authorized dealer for incidental WST operating costs, supported by CBS hedge-purpose documentation.

Offshore USD/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed by the group treasury entity at a Singapore or Hong Kong bank; no CBS approval applies to the non-resident IC, subject to board hedge authorization and ledger evidence of underlying CNY exposure.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/CNY, USD/EUR, USD/GBP) executed centrally by the upstream treasury vehicle in a recognized financial hub, not by the Samoa entity, to maintain a clean legal-entity FX position in the WS_IC.
Embedded hedges in SaaS and content-vendor contracts (fixed USD pricing, zero-cost collars, early-payment discounts) as natural substitutes for the thin offshore WST derivatives market.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Companies Registry (under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour / Samoa International Finance Authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee equals 10% of the annual license fee after a 30-day grace period; continued non-payment accrues a 5% monthly surcharge; deregistration may be initiated after 3 months of unpaid fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority – Compliance Office (AML/CFT Supervision)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the Annual Return on the incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of SAT 5,000 (approximately USD 1,850) plus continuing daily penalties; non-compliance may block license renewal and trigger a compliance review.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit for International Companies unless the company has publicly listed securities, holds a license under the International Insurance Act, or the Registrar issues a direction based on an investor complaint.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for listed or regulated entities; Samoa Equivalent IFRS accepted for local reporting; International Companies are only required to maintain internal accounting records sufficient to explain transactions and financial position.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Register of Beneficial Owners must be updated within 14 days of any ownership change. At each anniversary, the Annual Return must include a director's certification that the register has been maintained, reviewed, and that current beneficial ownership information remains accurate; an integrated UBO confirmation is thereby submitted with the Annual Return.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – 1,000 per annum (includes registered office, registered agent, and miscellaneous filing support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 – exempt from statutory audit; voluntary audit market rate USD 2,500 – 5,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Samoa International Companies are exempt from income tax on all foreign-source income under the International Companies Act 1987, as amended. No Samoan withholding tax applies to dividends or distributions paid by an International Company.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (Form IC-AR); filed via the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) e-Services portal. No corporate income tax return is required for a tax-exempt Samoa International Company.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Return and annual license fee are due within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation. Financial statements are not filed unless the company is licensed or required by SIFA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Remit through the registered agent; non-payment causes penalty and striking-off.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of compliance with International Companies Act and applicable Economic Substance Regulations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State that the company has not conducted taxable activity in Samoa unless it has claimed tax residency.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or late fee payment triggers a penalty of up to 10% of the annual fee, plus daily accruals. Continued default may result in deregistration and additional penalties against directors under SIFA practice.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa has a limited treaty network. A Samoa International Company is tax-exempt, so no Samoan withholding tax is imposed on dividends. If treaty relief is sought in another jurisdiction, the protocol is: (1) obtain a Samoa tax residency certificate from the Ministry of Revenue if the company is tax resident; (2) submit the treaty relief form to the payor or withholding agent in the shareholder's jurisdiction; (3) provide the TRC and an applicable IRS Form W-8 or equivalent before the payment date.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory domestic Samoa withholding tax on royalty and interest remittances to non-residents is 15%. However, an International Company is exempt from withholding obligations where the income is foreign-sourced. Treaty-reduced rates may apply under any applicable DTA, though Samoa has no comprehensive DTA with major commercial counterpart jurisdictions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa's Income Tax Act 2015 requires documentation for cross-border related-party transactions exceeding WST 10 million per annum (approximately USD 3.6 million). In practice, this threshold rarely applies to a tax-exempt International Company unless it has claimed tax residency or operates a taxable presence in Samoa.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa Economic Substance Regulations require International Companies that generate relevant core income to demonstrate adequate physical presence, employees, expenditure, and management in Samoa if they claim tax residency or treaty benefits. For a voice streaming and interactive social application, the relevant category is likely 'Provision of Other Core Income-Generating Activities' or telecommunication-type services; a purely non-resident-operated exempt IC may have no substance requirement but must not claim treaty residency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming exemption while operating a voice streaming app with a Samoan management office or permanent establishment that creates Samoan-source income; failing to declare actual taxable presence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid tax, penalties up to 150% of the tax shortfall, and daily late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Knowing directors may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax; criminal conviction may carry imprisonment and a travel ban.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a shell nominee without substance, or claiming economic substance compliance where none exists, to channel streaming revenues through Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Striking-off of the International Company, revocation of registration, and monetary penalties imposed by SIFA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be disqualified from acting as officers in Samoa and personally fined for signing false declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing proceeds from voice streaming fraud, money laundering, or activities connected to sanctioned persons; failing to maintain beneficial ownership records or appoint a compliance officer under Samoa AML/CFT law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to USD 100,000 per violation, asset freezing and forfeiture, account detention, and suspicious transaction reporting orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face criminal prosecution with imprisonment of 3 to 7 years, travel restrictions, and personal civil asset recovery.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Annual Return and License Fee Default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the IC Annual Return or to pay the annual license fee for more than 6 months.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic striking-off from the International Companies Register; late restoration requires settlement of all arrears and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for outstanding license fees and penalties; administrative disqualification may also apply.
